voiceover: Check your invitation on a guest's phone before you send. Four checks. Number three is the one people skip. You know your wedding invitation too well to see it fresh. Your guests will see it on a phone. See it there first. I'll use a Wedillybird demo for Léa and Adam, a fictional couple. One: use a phone that isn't yours, and open the link. Does the envelope open, and does the invitation appear? Look for the skip button, too. Two: read the names, the date and the venue out loud. Every name spelled right. The date. The place. The countdown. Scroll like a guest. Can you find the venue without help? Here's the part people skip: the reply. Three: try every answer, not just yes. Tap each answer in turn: I'll be there, Maybe, I can't make it. See what opens. Each guest should see only the plus-ones you allowed. If this helps, follow. One check to go. On your own invitation, stop before Send, so no real answer gets saved. Now read the dietary box the way a guest would. One limit to know about that box. It's a plain text box, so guests can write anything. If you need guests to pick a meal, you'd add a custom question. Custom questions are a Premium option. Either way, give guests with severe allergies a number to call. Four: hand it to someone who doesn't know the plan. Say nothing, and watch where they hesitate. Wherever they pause, your wording needs work. A borrowed phone. The details. Every answer. A cold read. Follow Wedillybird, and see a sample invitation: link in bio. I'm Norah, Wedillybird's AI host. That wraps our first fifteen days. Check it first, then send.

caption:
Digital wedding invitation: check it on a guest's phone before you send.
Four checks on a demo invitation: a borrowed phone, the details, every answer and a cold read. Léa and Adam are a fictional couple.
Hosted by Norah, an AI character created by the Wedillybird team.
pinned_comment: The pre-send check: 1) A phone that isn't yours: does the envelope open? 2) Read the names, date and venue out loud. 3) Try every answer (I'll be there, Maybe, I can't make it) and check the plus-ones; on your own invitation, stop before Send. 4) Hand it to someone who doesn't know the plan and say nothing. For meal choices, add a custom question (Premium). For severe allergies, give guests a number to call. Norah is AI-generated. Screens shown are real Wedillybird screens (demo data).
comment_bait: What's the first thing you'd check on your invitation?

sources.fact: Ask about allergies with a specific line; offer a way to reach the hosts for anything severe; meal choice is a separate question
sources.title: 25 Must-Ask Wedding RSVP Questions

sources.fact: Guests mark their entree choice on the response card; the reply card carries the hosts' contact line
sources.title: How to Word a Wedding Response Card

sources.fact: The invitation defines who is invited: show only the plus-ones you mean ('Wedding invitations are not negotiations')
sources.title: Handling your guests with grace (2008 column)

sources.fact: Pre-filled guest counts and clear addressing make the list clear
sources.title: How to Word Wedding Invitations

needs_proof: Founder (H51 caveat in r1b): confirm a host can actually open a guest's link on a second phone (preview link or test send) before this is filmed or posted. The script only says 'open the link' and never says how the link reaches a phone.
'Stop before Send, so no real answer gets saved' assumes nothing is stored until Send is pressed (convex/rsvps.ts); the demo itself stores nothing (r3 D1).
'Look for the skip button' (r3 B1) and 'a plain text box' (dietary needs, free text, r3 B1) must match the S01 and S04 captures.
'Custom questions are a Premium option' per r3 B1 (custom RSVP questions: Premium/Pro, up to ten questions, including single choice such as meals).
claims_review.notes: No figures: 'four checks' and 'fifteen days' are structure, not statistics. The only product limit is that the dietary field is free text; set meal choices need a Premium custom question. The allergy-contact and plus-one-clarity tips are Norah's suggestions drawing on T33 and T34 (vendor and etiquette guides), so no publisher is named on screen. No claim about how links are delivered. Wedillybird is named three times (beats 5, 28, 29).
